actual_call_path.probe: A bounded local probe serialized small valid collections and substituted Integer.MAX_VALUE for the serialized size. Guava 21.0 MapMakerInternalMap and all three tested vulnerable classes in 33.6.0-jre produced OutOfMemoryError under a 64 MiB heap. In 33.7.2-jre, CompactHashMap/Set rejected the truncated crafted stream with OptionalDataException after bounded allocation, and MapMakerInternalMap deserialized normally.
actual_call_path.vanilla_network: Exact bytecode captures for 1.14.4, 1.21.10, and 26.3 show the vanilla inbound pipeline constructing Minecraft PacketDecoder and decoding the protocol-specific ByteBuf through Minecraft packet codecs. These sampled paths do not use Java ObjectInputStream. The remaining 45 versions have literal-reference scan evidence but not individually traced control flow.
actual_call_path.vulnerability_mechanism: The vulnerable readObject implementations use a serialized element count to initialize collection capacity. The advisory identifies attacker-controlled oversized lengths as an uncontrolled memory allocation path. The upstream patch caps initial capacity at min(elementCount, 256) in CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet, and MapMakerInternalMap.

advisory.summary: Google Guava: CompactHashMap/CompactHashSet/MapMakerInternalMap deserialization triggers uncontrolled memory allocation

options: Use a compatible Minecraft runtime manifest containing Guava 33.7.2 or later, after upstream game compatibility validation.
Evaluate a supported launcher-side classpath replacement only with full game and mod compatibility checks.
compatible_remediation.owner: Mojang controls these runtime library pins. The mod source/build does not own or directly declare these versions.
compatible_remediation.reason: No safe project-controlled upgrade or verified launcher mitigation is established. No Minecraft-managed dependency override was added.

confidence: High for exact versions and component-level behavior; insufficient to conclude general reachability or non-reachability.

effective_configuration.minecraft: Package versions are pinned by official Minecraft version metadata and supplied as game runtime libraries.
effective_configuration.probe: Local process used -Xmx64m and -Xss256k. It made no network calls and did not connect to a game server.
effective_configuration.vanilla_client: The inspected default packet path is Minecraft typed packet decoding. Launcher classpaths, mod loader changes, third-party mods, custom serialization pipelines, and agents are not covered.

follow_up_requirements: Inspect exact supported launcher/runtime classpaths and loaded mods.
Trace any third-party Java deserialization or Netty ObjectDecoder pipeline reachable from attacker-controlled network data.
Request compatible Minecraft runtime updates and verify them before treating the advisory as resolved.

reachability_finding.conclusion: The Guava deserialization flaw is technically reproducible, but the reviewed evidence has not established an attacker-controlled Java deserialization path in the unmodified vanilla client. It also does not exclude third-party mods, launchers, reflection, or runtime instrumentation. The finding remains Further investigation and release-blocking.
reachability_finding.confidence: High for vulnerable/fixed version ranges, exact manifest ownership, artifact hashes, and bounded component-probe result; medium for literal-reference scan coverage; low for whole-process reachability under supported modded launchers because those environments were not observed.
reachability_finding.runtime_library_observation: The scan inspected 655 distinct official runtime library artifacts; 86 contain at least one of the targeted serialization-related strings. The generic Netty ObjectDecoder is present in runtime libraries in affected lines.
reachability_finding.vanilla_static_observation: The exact source-bound scan found no targeted Java serialization, Netty ObjectDecoder, or vulnerable Guava-class constant-pool references in any of 48 vanilla client binaries.

remaining_uncertainty: No production launcher classpaths or loaded mod lists were captured.
The scan is not whole-program data flow and does not resolve reflection or methods introduced by arbitrary mods.
No malicious Java serialization stream was injected through an actual supported game or mod network endpoint.
The 45 non-sampled client versions have literal-reference scans but not individual packet-decoder bytecode traces.

verified_mitigation.applied_to_minecraft: false; all observed Guava versions are Minecraft-managed and remain below the fixed version.
verified_mitigation.fixed_release: 33.7.2-jre is the first fixed release in the captured upstream advisory; the tested Maven artifact SHA-1/SHA-256 match Maven Central sidecars.
verified_mitigation.upstream_fix: The upstream Guava commit caps eager collection preallocation to 256 elements and adds malicious-stream regression cases.
